item.title: France: Protests "brought the entire population together for a common purpose"
item.description: This weekend, in cities across France, some 800,000 protesters, including students, railway workers and members of the Yellow Vest movement, took to the streets in largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations. Sparked by a month of high school student protests over educational inequality and crumbling school facilities, the movement has grown into a broader outcry over the cost of living, public spending and climate inaction, as people across France say they have reached their breaking point. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Who took part in Saturday's protests?
item.description: Weeks of student protests over poor conditions in schools and rising anger over the cost of living fuelled calls for a nationwide demonstration on October 17, bringing together youth activists and supporters of the Yellow Vest movement. The main grievance was the cost of living. The protesters demonstrating against it 'didn't get what they wanted', analyses France 24's Shirli Sitbon. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Who was behind the violence at Saturday's protests?
item.description: Violent clashes, fires, vandalism and looting marred demonstrations across France on Saturday as hundreds of thousands of people marched against the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools. The French Interior Ministry said about 400 people were arrested nationwide. Our partner TV station France 2 examined who was involved in the violence during Saturday's protests. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king. Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Condé Nast’s UK profits drop by more than a third as sale of Vogue publisher ruled out
item.description: Magazine group points to restructuring bill but says it ‘remains profitable in the UK for another year’ Profits at Condé Nast’s UK arm slumped by more than a third last year, according to figures published shortly after the billionaire family that owns the luxury magazine group and titles from Vogue to GQ ruled out a sale. The publisher, which enjoyed a bumper 2024 after booking £64m in proceeds from the sale of its UK headquarters Vogue House in London, saw pre-tax profits excluding exceptional items tumble 36% from £28m that year to nearly £18m last year. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Mother left two sons out of her will after family dispute; New Jersey court sides with daughters
item.description: A New Jersey mother who initially planned to divide her estate equally among her four children changed her will in 2016, excluding both sons after their relationship deteriorated. Following her death in 2024, the sons challenged the decision, alleging that their sisters had influenced her. One daughter had been her sole caregiver since 1996. However, on October 16, 2026, a New Jersey appeals court upheld the revised will. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Demi Moore’s Idaho home has a river, mountain views and wild elk in her backyard
item.description: Demi Moore has chosen to settle in Hailey, Idaho, immersed in the enchanting landscape of Sun Valley. She revels in the outdoor experiences available at her riverside retreat, including swimming, kayaking, and fly-fishing throughout the summer months. Initially intended as a vacation haven, the property has become her permanent residence. The area seamlessly marries rustic allure with an artistic vibe, drawing in art lovers for gallery excursions. item.title: 5-year-old asks for a baseball field, Ohio dad spends $30,000 building one in backyard
item.description: An Ohio father spent nearly two years and around $30,000 building a baseball field in his backyard after his five-year-old son requested one. Jason Kidd transformed his property into a playing field with professional-grade clay, regulation bases and a raised pitcher's mound. Despite complaints from neighbours and unfinished additions, Kidd said the project was about spending time with his son and teaching him baseball. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Side Hustle Grows Steadily: $500 yard games fund Little Party Co.; she keeps corporate job
item.description: Vanessa Romano launched Little Party Co. with just a $500 investment in outdoor party games, inspired by social media trends. Within a few months, her savvy approach catapulted her revenue to over $9,000. She strategically reinvested her profits while balancing a full-time corporate career and family.
